The `source` array uses simple string variable expansion (\$pkgname, \$pkgver, \$url) that resolves to the package's own declared upstream GitHub repository (https://github.com/llamastash/llamastash/archive/refs/tags/v0.6.1.tar.gz) — this is standard packaging practice and involves no command execution.

The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions contain the actual build and installation logic (cargo fetch, cargo build, install commands), but these functions are NOT executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` — only sourced as function definitions. There is no top-level command substitution, no `eval`, no base64 decoding, no network downloads or execution triggered at the global scope, and no obfuscated or encoded strings. Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe.</details>

This PKGBUILD is a standard, well-formed build script for the llamastash Rust application. The prepare() and build() functions use only cargo (fetch --locked, build --frozen --release) with an explicit stable toolchain, and the package() function installs the compiled binary and license/doc files into standard FHS locations ($pkgdir/usr/bin, $pkgdir/usr/share/licenses, $pkgdir/usr/share/doc).

There is no evidence of obfuscation, encoded commands, eval, base64-decoded payloads, or downloads/executions from unrelated hosts. The only network activity is cargo's normal resolution of dependencies from crates.io, which is standard for Rust packaging. The file does not modify unrelated system files, exfiltrate data, or contain backdoors.

Minor hygiene notes: the package is rebuilt on every install (no -bin prebuilt variant), and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable pins the Rust version, which is reasonable. These are packaging-style considerations, not security threats.
